title: As-Sabur, the Most Patient
tomorrow: Jordan asks Dadi: what do you call God when it's just you?

lines: DADI. CAN WE PLEASE JUST GO?
cards: Moving day. The truck said morning, and it's past lunch.
The tape has run out, the phone is nearly dead, and Dadi keeps stopping in each empty room of her apartment, touching the door frame, saying something under her breath.
Amira, holding the last box, hears her own voice come out sharp: "Dadi. Can we please just go?" Dadi goes quiet. A sentence like that is out before anyone decides to say it.
So what is patience, if it's always one second too late?

teach.h: NO ONE MORE PATIENT THAN ALLAH.
teach.b: Today's Name, the last of the traditional ninety-nine, is As-Sabur, the Most Patient. A hadith gives it a startling picture: no one is more patient with hurtful words than Allah.
People say He has a son, the hadith says, and still He gives them health and provision. Insulted, and still feeding the one who insults. That's the scale of it.
Then a story at human size.
The Prophet, peace be upon him, passed a woman weeping at a grave and told her to be mindful of Allah and patient. Not recognizing him, she snapped: leave me alone.
When she learned who it was, she came to his door to apologize.

teach.h: PATIENCE IS AT THE FIRST STRIKE.
teach.b: He told her: patience is at the first strike. That's the answer to the hook. Patience isn't the calm that arrives an hour later.
It's the first second, the one Amira missed. And the woman at the grave missed it too, and she still came back.
The Qur'an gives the help for both moments, in Surah al-Baqarah: "Seek help in steadfastness and prayer. Lo! Allah is with the steadfast."
Here's the thing to tell a friend: Pickthall's word there, steadfastness, is the same Arabic word as patience, sabr. Patience in this tradition isn't sitting still. It's standing firm.

how: Muslims say inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un at a sudden loss, often the first words at the first strike, and ask Allah for sabr in du'a.

o: the Silent, who never answers what people say to Him
the Most Patient, who keeps giving to those who wrong Him
the Slow, who waits a long time before He acts at all

games.q: what patience is — tap the pairs.

s: patience means calming down once the hard moment has passed
the hadith puts it earlier: patience is at the first strike.
a hadith says no one is more patient with hurtful words than Allah
people say He has a son, and still He gives them health and provision.

games.q: a friend asks: 'if God is so patient, why doesn't He just shut down the people who insult Him?' what does today's hadith say?
o: He hears them and still gives them health and provision; that's His patience.
He doesn't hear insults at all; He's far too high above them to notice.
He does stop them at once; patience is a virtue meant only for people.
games.why: the hadith says no one is more patient with hurtful words than Allah: insulted, He keeps providing.

practice: Find the most annoying sound near you: a fridge hum, traffic, someone else's video. Listen to it for the whole sit without trying to fix it or leave it. Each time you want to, that's a first strike; stay one more breath.

wordCard.voice: As-Sabur. The Most Patient, who keeps giving to the very people who wrong Him.

orig.note: Arabic: the Most Patient, the last Name in the traditional list; sabr is patience.

carryVoice: Here is the line: patient, at the first strike, and if you miss it, at the second. Ninety-nine of ninety-nine, complete.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 7378; Sahih Muslim 2804 (no one is more patient with hurtful words than Allah)
Sahih al-Bukhari 1283; Sahih Muslim 926 (the woman at the grave: patience is at the first strike)

sources.q: Seek help in steadfastness and prayer. Lo! Allah is with the steadfast.
